newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian residential property sector seen bullish.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian residential property sector seen bullish.

text.p: Sales of residential property in Malaysia are picking up following the setback last year of government measures to curb speculation, analysts say.

"We are positive about the outlook for the residential property sector. There has been a marked improvement with sales in certain areas picking up substantially," said a property analyst with a foreign brokerage.
He said the sector seemed to have weathered the stiff curbs on property transactions announced last year.
The curbs include a 100,000 ringgit ($40,000) levy on purchases by foreigners who also have to pay a flat property sales tax of 30 percent, instead of a previous sliding rate of five to 20 percent.
Earlier, the central bank limited loans for second property purchases to 60 percent.

"People are starting to buy again after realising that prices were not coming down," said a Mayban Securities analyst. "The short to medium term outlook is good. We particularly like companies which are developing townships."
He said the sell-off in stocks of property companies after the imposition of the measures was due to sentiment rather than earnings concerns.

An official at property consultant Rahim & Co Research said demand would continue to outstrip the supply of landed residential properties over the next few years, helped by the buoyant Malaysian economy.
But analysts were less optimistic about the outlook for the commercial property sector.

"The commercial property sector does not look very promising. There has already been a glut in office and retail spaces in Kuala Lumpur and it will only get worse with the completion of more high-rise buildings," said the foreign brokerage analyst.
Major property projects in the capital include the Kuala Lumpur City Centre which will comprise a complex of 22 office buildings -- including the Petronas Towers, the world's tallest buildings.
Although most analysts rated the overall property sector as "neutral", they recommended an overweighting in stocks of companies involved mainly in landed residential property development.
These include IOI Properties Bhd, Asas Dunia Bhd, Peladang Kimia Bhd and Land & General Bhd.
